title: ICE Agent Christian Castro Released From Texas Jail; State Charges Remain Unresolved
excerpt: ICE agent Christian Castro — charged with felony assault and filing a false police report for the January shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant in Minneapolis — was released from a Texas county jail after reaching the 90-day detention limit, with Texas Governor Abbott having refused to extradite him to Minnesota.
content:
On August 27, 2026, ICE agent Christian Castro was released from the Carrizales-Rucker Cameron County Detention Center in Brownsville, Texas, at 6:59 a.m., after reaching the 90-day limit on fugitive detention under Texas law.

Castro faces four counts of second-degree felony assault and one count of falsely reporting a crime in Hennepin County, Minnesota. Prosecutors allege he shot Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, 24, in the leg through the front door of a Minneapolis home during an immigration operation on January 14, 2026, and then falsely accused Sosa-Celis and another man of attacking ICE officers with a broom handle and a snow shovel — claims later disproven by video evidence.

  • Texas Governor Greg Abbott refused to sign the extradition paperwork, and a federal judge the day before had declined to intervene.
  • Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison had filed a lawsuit to force the extradition; Minnesota officials said they feared Castro could flee to Mexico.
  • Federal prosecutors separately considered but ultimately declined to charge Castro with federal civil rights violations, according to a report published on August 30.
  • Castro's release without extradition drew criticism from Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty and Minnesota officials.

The case marked a significant test of whether state criminal accountability for federal immigration agents could be enforced across state lines, with the outcome representing a significant failure of that accountability mechanism.
source: PBS NewsHour / Al Jazeera / Minnesota Reformer
